text: As the Patriots prepare to head to Jacksonville for a Week 3 AFC showdown against the Jaguars, the team faces a mounting injury crisis that threatens to derail what's been an inconsistent start to the season—Mike Onwenu's broken right ankle represents a significant blow to the offensive line, while safety Dell Pettus has been placed on injured reserve, though there's a measure of good news with rookie tight end Eli Raridon returning to practice. The Patriots have made corresponding roster moves, promoting linebacker Jose Ramirez from the practice squad to the 53-man roster and signing linebacker Benton Whitley to the practice squad, but the real challenge lies in execution: Jacksonville's defense is expected to rely heavily on Cover-6 looks, which the Patriots must solve by building on their "X" plays, while the team has also admitted to poor clock management before halftime in recent weeks—a pattern that needs correcting against a Jaguars team that's hungry for a response after their worst offensive performance in eleven months.
